Lessons.Title: Multiply Two-digit Numbers and One-digit Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will multiply a two-digit number and a one-digit number using place value understanding.
In the previous lesson, you solved two-digit multiplication problems in a way that made sense to them. You discussed decomposing factors and considered different representations of your strategy. In this lesson, you extend these ideas to find the value of products beyond 100, focusing on representations and strategies based on place value and the properties of operations, which are familiar from grade 3.
Core relationship: Multiply two-digit by one-digit numbers. Break two-digit number into tens and ones; multiply and add partial products.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Notice and Wonder: With and Without a Grid	 (10 minutes); Activity 1: Tyler's Diagrams (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Two Kinds of Diagrams	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Represent the Product	 (5 minutes)
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

WorkedExamples.Question: Find 47 × 6.
WorkedExamples.Method: Break two-digit number into tens and ones; multiply and add partial products.
Steps: Identify all quantities and common units.
Confirm 282 by the inverse or a visual model.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dropping the product contributed by the tens.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Break two-digit number into tens and ones; multiply and add partial products.
